subject: Hospitality
title: The Turnaround: Flipping Event Spaces
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Turnaround: Flipping Event Spaces usable.

hook.text: A ballroom hosts a conference at 5 PM, then transforms into a gala dinner by 7 PM.

buildup.text: Turnaround crews remove 500 theater chairs, set 60 round tables with linens, arrange centerpieces, reset AV, and adjust lighting.

discovery.text: Hotels charge $5,000–20,000 for turnarounds. The labor, speed, and precision required justify the premium.

twist.text: A delayed turnaround visibly fails: guests arrive to see staff still working, tablecloths half-set.

climax.text: The best banquet teams rehearse turnarounds with the precision of theater stagehands.

punchline.text: 500 chairs out, 60 tables in, 90 minutes. The turnaround is hospitality's ultimate sprint.

quiz.question: What is a 'turnaround' in hotel event operations?
options: Rapidly transforming an event space from one setup to another between events
